This is a repo for a web server library in C. We tend to prefer using header files when possible to make things easier to include for library users

Here’s a concise overview of the repo and what it’s trying to do:

- What this is
  - A C web server library implemented as headers (header-first design) with a small runtime server core (CServer) and accompanying utilities.

- Core components
  - CServer.h
    - Hash-map (Map) and generic list (List) data structures.
    - Lightweight TCP/UDP socket abstractions (TCPSocket, UDPSocket) and helper routines.
    - A multi-threaded HTTP server core (CServer) with:
      - A listening socket thread and a pool of worker threads.
      - Thread-safe request queue (List of OpenSocket items).
      - Extensible security hooks (rate limiter and security_function).
      - A pluggable request handler (handler_function).
    - Handy management helpers (start/stop server, memory cleanup, etc.).
  - test.c
    - A minimal example showcasing starting the HTTP server, responding with a body, and stopping when a condition is met in the request body.
  - UDP/TCP utilities
    - Basic interfaces for creating, cleaning up, sending/receiving via TCP/UDP.

- Project structure and artifacts
  - chat.json: one-line repo purpose (header-centric C web server library).
  - README.md: notes on open-source, single-header design, embedded-friendly goals, and WIP status.
  - test_exe: placeholder (no real binary yet).
  - test.sh: small curl-based test client.
  - Make/configs
    - make: a tiny, non-standard makefile snippet showing EXECUTABLE_NAME and FILE.
  - VSCode config
    - .vscode/settings.json: file-type associations to treat many headers as C.
    - .vscode/launch.json and tasks.json: debugging and build task setup (Bear Make workflow).

- How to use (high level)
  - Create a CServer via c_server_start_http_options or c_server_start_http.
  - Provide a handler_function to generate HTTP responses.
  - Provide security hooks (rate limiter and security_function).
  - Run the server (it will spawn a socket thread and worker threads); shut down via c_server_stop and free resources with c_server_free.

- Current status and caveats
  - The project is a work in progress (unlicense, header-based library, embedded-friendly).
  - Memory management pitfalls to watch for:
    - Thread-argument lifetimes (ThreadWorkerData) and who frees it.
    - Potential double-frees or use-after-free if lifecycles aren’t carefully synchronized.
    - Ensuring all heap-allocated resources owned by the server are freed in all code paths.
  - UDP/TCP server code is present but not fully fleshed out in all spots (e.g., some stubs and comments).

- Suggested next steps (if you want to move forward)
  - Stabilize lifecycle: lock down ownership for per-thread data (who frees ThreadWorkerData and when).
  - Add clean, single destructor paths for server and worker data to avoid leaks.
  - Expand tests: a small test suite validating creation, request handling, and shutdown.
  - Improve documentation: tiny usage guide and API notes for Map/List and CServer.
  - Consider making the library more header-only or providing a simple compile script to build a test executable.

If you want, I can tailor a quick developer-friendly patch plan (or a drop-in patch) to fix the lifecycle issues and add a minimal unit test around the worker thread data.

We diagnosed a double-free in TCP socket cleanup, clarified that pthread_join doesn’t free pthread_t, and outlined ownership models for per-thread ThreadWorkerData to enable safe, predictable cleanup.
